sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Deep-Sea Tugboat Towage and Maritime Emergency Salvage Contracts

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: None identified as in force: the Marshall Islands is not a party to a standalone bilateral investment treaty, double taxation avoidance agreement, or preferential trade agreement relevant to this incorporation; the US-RMI Compact of Free Association governs economic relations but is not a tax treaty or BIT.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of the Marshall Islands Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012, as amended; Business Corporations Act, Title 33 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code, as amended, including mandatory beneficial ownership record-keeping by licensed registered agents; Registrar of Corporations Guidance on Beneficial Ownership; and the Criminal Offenses provisions of Title 15, Marshall Islands Revised Code, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity document for each proposed director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing government authority of the individual's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) where the issuing state is a Convention party; otherwise consular legalization through an RMI consular authority or Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Marshall Islands licensed registered agent and incorporation service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the jurisdiction where executed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization chain, verified by the RMI registered agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and AML compliance certificate in respect of each shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or financial institution maintaining the relevant account relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed by authorized bank officer and notarized; if demanded by the RMI registered agent, apostilled or consular legalized in the issuing jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate resolution and certificate of good standing for any corporate shareholder or UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or corporate registry in the corporate shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consular legalization cover sheet / registry attestation for foreign public documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or honorary consular office in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization following the foreign ministry chain of the issuing country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit domestic watchlist, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and other OFAC sanctions lists, FATF and APG high-risk jurisdiction lists, and applicable EU/UK HM Treasury sanctions. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, family member, or close associate; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence must be independently corroborated, with senior management approval before acceptance. For the ISIC 5222 marine towage and emergency salvage sector, heightened scrutiny applies to Lloyd's Open Form payments, casualty-related disbursements, cash at sea, and distress-port disbursements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry (Registrar of Corporations), Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands; non-resident Business Corporation name clearance is submitted through a licensed registered agent, with no general public online filing portal for this entity type.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English or Marshallese using Latin/Roman alphabet characters. There is no mandatory transliteration into a local script. The name must be distinguishable from all registered names and may not be misleading or imply a nonexistent relationship with the RMI government, a licensed profession, or a regulated financial activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 30-day period upon written request and payment of the prescribed renewal fee. If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant may, within 14 calendar days of the refusal, submit a written Notice of Administrative Appeal and revised submissions to the Registrar of Corporations; the Registrar shall issue a decision within 5 working days. A further appeal lies to the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, which must be filed within 30 calendar days of the Registrar's final refusal, accompanied by a legal memorandum, evidence of legitimate interest, and any relevant trademark or business-name registration. If no appeal is filed, a fresh name clearance application may be submitted after 30 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not acceptable as the statutory registered office for a Marshall Islands non-resident Business Corporation engaged in ISIC 5222 offshore towage and salvage. The corporation must continuously maintain a physical registered office in the Republic of the Marshall Islands through a licensed registered agent. A virtual address may be used only as an auxiliary correspondence or vessel-operational mailing point, never as the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate, approximately 10-15% per examination cycle for unannounced inspections of the registered agent's office and UBO records by the Registrar or RMI Financial Intelligence Unit. For the deep-sea towage and emergency salvage operations, the inspection risk is elevated: approximately 60-70% for flag State, Port State Control, casualty-triggered, and class-related physical inspections of tugs and salvage vessels.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and availability search fee for a non-resident Business Corporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations via licensed registered agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization of UBO identity and corporate documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed registered agent and registered office first-year fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for non-resident Business Corporation; typical range USD 1,200-1,800

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registrar of Corporations / RMI National Treasury

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC, PEP, sanctions screening, and UBO declaration compliance package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent / RMI AML compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed compliance fee, equivalent to USD 150-250 per hour for professional review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation of articles of incorporation, bylaws, corporate resolutions, and registered agent consent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed legal fee benchmark for non-resident Business Corporation formation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, codified at 27 MIRC Chapter 1; Sections 5 and 6 (Certificate of Incorporation), Sections 7 and 8 (Registered Agent and Registered Office), Sections 25 to 29 (Directors and Officers), and Section 36 (Share Issuance).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation (Articles of Incorporation) filed with the Registrar of Corporations
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account requirement; the corporation may issue one or more no-par value shares and capital may remain fully unpaid, with at least one share subscribed for organizational validity. Non-resident domestic corporations are exempt from domestic income tax and business license tax.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription for one thousand (1,000) no-par value common shares is approved and the Secretary is directed to issue share certificates to the initial subscriber and to enter the issuance in the share transfer ledger. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the office of the designated registered agent in Majuro is adopted as the Corporation's registered office, and the registered agent is authorized to receive legal process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are appointed officers: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve until their successors are elected. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to execute contracts, open bank accounts, and obtain the necessary maritime towage and salvage licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro (online registry portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the proposed corporate name with a corporate suffix such as 'Corporation', 'Inc.', or 'Limited'; verify that the name is distinguishable from all registered entities in the Marshall Islands registry; pay the name reservation fee and obtain the reservation certificate valid for sixty (60) days.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for confusion or similarity with an existing entity, the applicant may submit a revised name request or file a written consent from the conflicting entity to the Registrar within ten (10) business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent on behalf of the Office of the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Certificate of Incorporation containing the corporate name, registered agent name, registered office address in Majuro, authorized share capital with no-par value shares, the broad purpose clause covering deep-sea towage and maritime salvage, and the incorporator details; execute the certificate before a notary public or the attested signature of the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation drafted in English
Consent to act as registered agent
Proof of registered office address in Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is returned by the Registrar for deficiencies, correct the noted defects in the filing package and resubmit within five (5) business days; a notice of correction will specify the exact amendments required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Submission to the Registrar and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Certificate of Incorporation together with the registered agent's consent and the government filing fee through the licensed registered agent; the Registrar verifies the filing, assigns a unique corporate registration number, and endorses the certificate. The incorporation becomes effective on the date of filing.
required_dossiers: Government filing fee payment receipt (bank draft or electronic transfer)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or defect notice, the registered agent must file a corrective amendment with the Registrar and pay the applicable amendment fee; the incorporation is perfected upon the Registrar's acceptance of the corrected filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting or obtain unanimous written consent of the incorporator and initial directors to adopt the bylaws, ratify the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and officer appointments, and issue share certificates to the initial subscriber; record all documents in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or unanimous written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the organizational documents contain inconsistencies or omissions, the directors may execute a corrective written consent to ratify the actions and the registered agent will maintain such consent in the corporate records; no public filing is required for internal governance documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax-Exempt Status Confirmation and Certificate of Good Standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations and Marshall Islands Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the corporation qualifies as a non-resident domestic corporation exempt from Marshall Islands income tax and business license tax; apply for a Certificate of Good Standing from the Registrar and, where requested by banking or contractual counterparties, obtain an official tax exemption certificate; settle any annual franchise tax or filing fees to maintain active status.
required_dossiers: Application for Certificate of Good Standing
Annual franchise tax payment receipt if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Good Standing is queried due to unpaid fees or missing filings, pay all outstanding franchise taxes and penalties, file any overdue annual reports, and resubmit the application with official payment receipts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Marshall Islands Maritime Administrator (MIMA) under the Republic of the Marshall Islands Maritime Act 1990, acting through the Marine Safety Division of International Registries, Inc. (IR)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Ship Registry and Offshore Towing and Salvage Operating License

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A (Full EIA Report) is required for wreck removal or salvage operations conducted inside lagoon or reef-protected waters; Category B (EIA Registration) applies to open-ocean towage and emergency salvage, subject to EPA screening and written confirmation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL 73/78 Annexes I (oil), IV (sewage), V (garbage), and VI (air emissions); zero discharge of oil or harmful substances in the exclusive economic zone; adherence to IMO Ballast Water Management Convention standards; allowable VOC, NOx, and SOx emission limits per MEPC requirements; waste handling under the Basel Convention where transboundary movement of salvage waste occurs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for vessel machinery spaces and accommodation quarters; SOLAS and ISM Code Safety Management Certificate; ISPS Code Ship Security Certificate; structural load and stability inspection for towing hooks, winches, and deck fittings; crew certificates of competency and medical fitness; port state control clearance from the RMI Marine Safety Division; workplace safety clearance under the applicable labor standards and Maritime Labour Convention obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Treasury, Revenue and Customs divisions); official government portal: https://www.rmi.gov.mh. Customs administration: Marshall Islands Customs and Excise Service. Corporate registry: Office of the Registrar of Corporations under the Business Corporations Act 1990 (filings through licensed registered agents; no public self-service e-TIN portal).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The RMI levies no general income tax and no VAT, so there is no statutory TIN or VAT-ID issuance for foreign entities. The operational sequence for an offshore towage/salvage Business Corporation is: (1) incorporate under the Business Corporations Act 1990 through an RMI-licensed registered agent and obtain the Certificate of Registration and corporate registration number; (2) adopt the non-resident domestic corporation status by board resolution confirming that all towage/salvage operations are conducted outside the RMI and file the status with the Registrar; (3) do not apply for a fiscal TIN - none is required or issued for non-resident entities; (4) if the vessel calls at RMI ports or imports duty-free stores, register with the Marshall Islands Customs and Excise Service for a customs importer/exporter reference code; (5) if the operator employs RMI-resident crew or maintains an RMI shore office, register with the RMI Social Security Administration for an employer number and with the municipal government for a business license. A pure foreign-going, RMI-flagged tug operator completes steps (1) and (2) only and pays the annual non-resident registration fee of approximately USD 500.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box, passthrough election, or hybrid-mismatch election exists under RMI tax law because the RMI has no income tax, no branch profits tax, and no CFC/anti-hybrid regime. The only relevant statutory designation is the 'Non-Resident Domestic Corporation' status available under the Business Corporations Act 1990: a corporation that resolves to carry on no business within the Republic except activities incidental to its offshore status is excluded from all RMI taxes, duties (other than the annual registration fee), and municipal business license requirements. An existing domestic corporation may elect non-resident status by filing an amendment to its articles and registered-agent certificate; the status lapses if the corporation resumes physical business in RMI, in which case the tax exemption is prospectively and, on audit, retrospectively lost. Foreign maritime entities operating RMI-flagged tugs may alternatively register under the Maritime Act, but that registration is a flag/concession mechanism, not a tax election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None - the Republic of the Marshall Islands imposes no VAT, GST, or national sales-and-use tax; indirect fiscal measures are limited to customs/excise import duties, municipal business license fees, and social security contributions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - there is no VAT/GST regime and therefore no economic-turnover registration threshold. From a customs perspective, any importer/exporter must be representable by a licensed customs agent or hold an importer/exporter reference code under the Customs and Excise Act, irrespective of turnover. If the operator carries on physical business inside the RMI (e.g., in-port or coastal towage, crew agency, shore office), the municipal Business License Act 1989 requires an annual business license, with fees graduated by gross receipts band.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The RMI has no mandatory e-invoicing, no real-time fiscal clearance API, no digital stamping, and no continuous transaction controls. Customs declarations (export clearances, stores lists) are lodged with the Marshall Islands Customs and Excise Service on paper or through the available electronic cargo declaration system; this is a border control, not an indirect-tax clearance mandate. No cryptographic invoice authentication is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The statutory zero-rating concept does not exist because the RMI has no VAT/GST. In substance, offshore towage and salvage services performed by an RMI non-resident BC (e.g., Lloyd's Open Form, SCOPIC, BIMCO Towcon/Towhire contracts) are outside the RMI tax base: services are deemed rendered abroad, remuneration is not subject to any RMI consumption tax, and no refund mechanism is needed. For goods, export duty-neutrality applies only if (a) goods are declared for export under the Customs and Excise Act, and (b) bunkers, stores, spare parts, and salvage gear on an RMI-flagged tug are covered by an inward/outward ship's stores list for a foreign-going voyage. RMI-flagged tug and barge units engaged in international salvage/towage may also claim customs relief on imported equipment used in the foreign trade where the Director of Customs approves the installation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed with the Marshall Islands Customs and Excise Service covering vessel stores, bunkers, spares, and salvage gear
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill for the towed convoy plus the towage/salvage service contract (Lloyd's Open Form/Towcon or Towhire)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT wire advice evidencing settlement of the Lloyds standard form remuneration into the RMI entity's bank account
Marshall Islands vessel registry certificate and class certificate for the tug (and towed unit registration where applicable)
Ship's stores list signed by the master, together with port clearance, for duty-free outward-bound treatment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: RMI has no VAT refund or export-zero-rating credit, so no statutory tax clawback of refunds can arise. The enforceable exposure is: (1) Customs fraud - false export declarations, false stores lists, or misdescription of salvage equipment expose the operator to forfeiture of the tug/cargo, a fine of up to twice the duty evaded, and an additional penalty not exceeding USD 10,000 under the Customs and Excise Act, with retrospective reassessment of duty on goods not validly exported; (2) Abuse of the non-resident tax-exempt status - if the Director of Customs or the Registrar determines the BC performed business within RMI (in-port towage, RMI crew payroll, local shore office), the exemption is void and municipal business license fees and penalties are assessed retrospectively from commencement, subject to judicial review in the RMI High Court; (3) FX settlement - the 180-day repatriation term is a banking/escrow and AML/CFT covenant rather than an exchange-control law (USD is legal tender and no exchange controls exist); failure to repatriate invoice proceeds within 180 days may trigger escrow penalties, wire-recall liability, and adverse audit findings, and can be treated as an annuality red flag for the enhanced due-diligence tier under the RMI AML/CTF regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands has no central bank; monetary and financial regulatory functions are administered by the Banking Commissioner within the Ministry of Finance and the Financial Action Taskforce-aligned supervisory framework of the Pacific International Bankers Association.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is legal tender and circulates freely; both capital and current account transactions are fully convertible with no statutory exchange controls, no central bank approval for inward or outward remittances, and no profit remittance restrictions. Dividends, service fees, and liquidation proceeds may be transferred abroad without exchange licensing, subject only to AML/CFT verification and bank-specific documentary review.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender obligation exists. There is no statutory timeline for converting export receipts into local currency because the U.S. dollar is the domestic means of exchange, and all salvage/towage revenue retained in USD or held offshore is unrestricted.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational USD account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. The RMI does not maintain a dedicated fintech or electronic money institution licensing regime for non-resident offshore EMIs; non-deposit-taking fintech platforms are not regulated as banks and cannot provide USD settlement infrastructure or Lloyd's Standard Form wire clearing. Any such arrangement must be structured as a pass-through payment agent, not as a licensed EMI, and would face high correspondent-bank friction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandated. At least one director and the designated signatory(ies) must attend an in-person onboarding interview at the bank's Majuro office or with a notarized offshore representative if permitted in writing by the Compliance Officer. Remote video onboarding is possible for renewal or limited-purpose accounts but is not standard for initial corporate account opening; a physical Board resolution, original corporate seal, and wet-ink signatures are normally required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity through nominee shareholders and bearer-like structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the corporate register, full chain of ownership up to the ultimate natural persons, trust deed and declaration of trust, director/shareholder registers, and a formal written explanation of the commercial rationale for each nominee layer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore maritime assets and cross-jurisdictional tug fleet flagged as higher-risk for sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid International Tonnage Certificate, Certificate of Registry from the Maritime Administrator, ISPS/MTSA compliance evidence, vessel-specific sanctions screening reports (OFAC/UN/EU), and charter party contracts showing the economic flow of each towage and salvage engagement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Irregular or lumpy salvage award settlements generating unexplained high-value wire activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lloyds Standard Form salvage agreement, salvage arbitration or SCOPIC evidence, published Lloyd's Open Form casualty number, invoice and payment waterfall, insurance certificate with P&I club confirmation, and audited financial statements demonstrating revenue recognition.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant USD wire via SWIFT MT103 from the beneficial owner's regulated bank account to the designated BOMI or Bank of Guam operational account. The wire must include a transparent purpose code such as 'Capital Contribution / Equity Injection' (general government purpose under the IMF Balance of Payments classification is not applicable because the RMI has no exchange control regime) and must be accompanied by a board resolution, signed equity subscription, and source-of-funds evidence from the remitter's banking institution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements are SWIFT MT103 payments for operational disbursements, commercial irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued by the vessel owner's bank to suppliers, and escrowed disbursements under Lloyds Standard Form where the salvage award is paid by the salvors' protection and indemnity club. All outbound wires must carry the correct underlying invoice reference, and payments to sanctioned or restricted jurisdictions are prohibited; bank-specific compliance review is applied to each clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-denominated forward contracts booked with an offshore correspondent bank for conversion of USD receipts into prudent operating currencies (e.g., AUD, NZD, JPY) where vessels incur crew, fuel, and port costs.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with a licensed Tier-1 international bank for USD/CAD or USD/EUR exposure arising from global salvage contracts, settled in USD without requiring local jurisdiction delivery.
Cross-currency swaps limited to EUR/USD or JPY/USD for long-duration towage contracts, provided transaction is single-purpose and collateral is posted as USD cash at an RMI licensed bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report under the Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before November 30 of each calendar year; the deadline is fixed by statute and is not tied to the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of USD 50 for reports submitted after November 30; a corporation that fails to file for two consecutive years becomes subject to administrative dissolution (strike-off) by the Registrar

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit thresholds exist under the Business Corporations Act; non-resident business corporations are not required to file financial statements or undergo an independent audit. Audits occur only if required by shareholder agreement, lender covenants, or insurance/underwriting arrangements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The Business Corporations Act does not mandate a specific accounting framework; financial statements voluntarily prepared by the corporation are conventionally presented under IFRS or US GAAP, with records maintained in US dollars.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Licensed registered agents must obtain and retain current beneficial ownership information for each client entity and must re-confirm the beneficial ownership schedule on an annual basis in connection with the Annual Report cycle. Any share transfer must be lodged with the registered agent (transfer instrument, board consent, and updated member register) so that the agent's beneficial ownership records are updated before the next annual confirmation; the agent's annual register audit reconciles the Register of Members, Register of Directors, and Minute Book against the Annual Report and current ownership records.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800–2,500 per annum for licensed registered agent, registered office, and corporate secretarial maintenance, exclusive of government fees
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; voluntary certified audit for a small offshore towage and salvage holding company typically ranges from USD 3,500–7,500 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-resident Business Corporation exempt from Marshall Islands income tax on foreign-source profits; no capital gains tax, no annual profits tax, no gross revenue tax; only a flat annual government franchise tax is payable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return exists. The compliance filing is the Business Corporation Annual Report (BC-AR) submitted through the RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations electronic portal (verify.rmioc.com).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 30 April of the year following the reporting calendar year; the annual report and annual government franchise tax must be filed and paid through the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 1 — Corporate Name and Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Business Corporation exactly as stated in the articles of incorporation and its RMI registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the registered BC legal name; no trading name may be substituted unless separately registered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 2 — Registered Agent and Registered Office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and street address of the licensed RMI registered agent and the registered office in the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident BC must maintain a licensed RMI registered agent and cannot serve as its own agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names and usual residential addresses of all directors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors may be non-resident; the BC must have at least one director, and nominee directors must be disclosed to the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number and classes of authorized and issued shares, including par value if any.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the share schedule from the articles; authorized share maximum may determine the annual government fee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Street address of the company's principal office, including the operational base for towage and salvage activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the actual operating address outside RMI; a post office box alone is not sufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 6 — Franchise Tax Declaration and Certification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the annual government franchise tax and certification by a director, officer, or registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No income, asset, or balance sheet details are disclosed; false certification is a criminal offense.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and non-payment of the annual government fee attract late penalties and daily surcharges under the Registrar's fee schedule; continued default may result in administrative dissolution or revocation of the certificate, and reinstatement requires payment of all arrears, penalties, and reinstatement fees.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network and does not issue tax residence certificates for income tax relief. Where a foreign jurisdiction requires proof of status, the RMI Registrar may issue a Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Corporate Existence; that certificate confirms registration and legal existence, not tax residence in a DTA sense.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory RMI withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest is 0%; inbound royalties and interest received by a non-resident Business Corporation are also outside RMI taxation. No treaty rates are available because no applicable double taxation treaty exists.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory threshold (USD 0); RMI law does not impose Local File or Master File obligations. Group-level CbCR thresholds in other jurisdictions may require the RMI entity to be identified as a constituent entity.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Marshall Islands Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to registered entities carrying on relevant activities, including shipping. Offshore towage and salvage operations may be treated as a shipping relevant activity for ESR purposes. A non-resident Business Corporation must either demonstrate economic substance in the Marshall Islands by maintaining local management and control, premises, employees, and records proportionate to the activity, or establish tax residence in another qualifying jurisdiction. Annual substance reporting is mandatory; non-compliance triggers financial penalties and deregistration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Marshall Islands Business Corporation to conceal profits actually sourced in the Marshall Islands, or making false declarations to foreign revenue authorities regarding residence, management, or tax status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: False filings to the Registrar are punishable under RMI law; registration may be revoked and the entity struck off. Foreign tax authorities may impose penalties, interest, and deny tax treaty or exemption benefits where the structure is a sham.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false reports or participate in evasion may be held personally liable for civil restitution, disqualified from acting as directors, and subject to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Business Corporation with no physical presence, no local registered office substance, no board oversight, and no genuine economic activity in RMI while carrying on a relevant towage, salvage, or shipping activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Economic Substance Regulations, the Registrar may impose a financial penalty of up to USD 10,000 plus up to USD 1,000 per day for continuing default, and may strike off or dissolve the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally liable for penalties if willful default is proven; courts may pierce the corporate veil where the entity is used as a mere façade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Sanctions / Beneficial Ownership Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the towage and salvage company to process payments through unvetted escrow arrangements or related-party wires connected to sanctioned persons, failing to maintain beneficial ownership records, or refusing to cooperate with the registered agent's AML verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI anti-money laundering laws provide for fines, forfeiture of vessels and proceeds, and imprisonment up to 10 years. The RMI Maritime Administrator may suspend, revoke, or refuse to renew the vessel's flag registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face civil forfeiture, travel bans, and extradition on money laundering or sanctions evasion charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Annual Report / Franchise Tax Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the Business Corporation Annual Report by 30 April and failing to pay the annual government franchise tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late penalties and daily surcharges accrue; continued non-compliance leads to administrative dissolution or revocation of registration. Reinstatement requires settlement of all unpaid fees, penalties, and reinstatement charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who breach their fiduciary duty by permitting non-filing may be liable to the company for resulting damages, and may be named in reinstatement proceedings before the Registrar.
